title: hs-Troponin 0/1-h Chest Pain Pathway
keywords: symptom onset >= 2 h HEART <= 3 no ischemic ECG
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Chest Pain / hs-cTn Algorithm (ESC 2023, AHA 2025)
ESC 2023 ACS guideline; 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline; PLATO; DETO2X-AMI

changelog.change: Initial entry — the 0/1-h hs-cTnI rule-out/rule-in table with the mandatory discharge caveats, plus the ACS management bundle. STEMI-equivalent ECG patterns are in twelve-lead-stemi-criteria.

summary: The 0/1-hour high-sensitivity troponin algorithm safely rules NSTEMI in or out in an hour — but only with BOTH samples, an assay it was validated for, symptom onset ≥ 2 hours ago, a low clinical risk score, and no ischaemic ECG change. Thresholds are assay-specific: the values below are hs-cTnI (Abbott ARCHITECT) — confirm your local assay.

body.text: Not for standard (non-high-sensitivity) troponin. Not a substitute for the ECG — a STEMI or STEMI-equivalent goes to the cath lab regardless of troponin (see twelve-lead-stemi-criteria).

rows: RULE IN — NSTEMI confirmed; admit + cardiology
RULE IN — NSTEMI regardless of the absolute value
OBSERVE — repeat troponin at 3 h; add a clinical risk score and re-examine the ECG

body.text: Do NOT discharge on a rule-out unless ALL of:

items: Symptom onset ≥ 2–3 h before the first sample (early presenters can have a falsely low initial value).
A low clinical risk score (e.g. HEART ≤ 3).
No new ischaemic ECG change (ST depression ≥ 0.5 mm, de Winter, Wellens, new LBBB).
No high-risk feature: ongoing rest pain > 20 min, exertional syncope, haemodynamic instability, new heart failure, a dynamic troponin in the observe zone.
Aspirin 324 mg PO chewed (non-enteric) on suspicion — only true allergy or active haemorrhage contraindicates.

P2Y12 inhibitor: ticagrelor 180 mg (preferred; PLATO). Prasugrel 60 mg only if PCI is planned and no prior stroke/TIA, age < 75, weight ≥ 60 kg. Practice on ED pre-treatment before known coronary anatomy varies — often given while a STEMI transfer is in progress, less so for NSTEMI going to next-day angiography.
Anticoagulation: unfractionated heparin 60 units/kg IV bolus (max 4000) then 12 units/kg/h (max 1000/h); or enoxaparin; bivalirudin for HIT.
Oxygen ONLY if SpO₂ < 90% — hyperoxia increases infarct size in normoxic patients (DETO2X-AMI, AVOID). Target 94–98%.

Nitroglycerin SL 0.4 mg q5min ×3 for ongoing pain; IV for hypertensive emergency or flash pulmonary oedema. AVOID in a right-ventricular infarct (JVD + hypotension + clear lungs — preload-dependent) and within 24–48 h of a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor.
Avoid morphine in NSTEMI — it delays P2Y12 absorption and is associated with worse outcomes (CRUSADE). Use fentanyl 25–50 mcg IV if analgesia is needed.
On oral anticoagulation (e.g. AF): after PCI, drop the aspirin early and use dual therapy (anticoagulant + clopidogrel) — less bleeding, similar ischaemic protection (AUGUSTUS, ENTRUST-AF PCI).
